items.t: PTC (PTC) Stock Looks Reasonable As A $205 Cash Deal Lands
sum: PTC Inc. has agreed to a US$205 per share cash takeover while its stock trades around US$195. That gap puts a spotlight on whether the current market price lines up with what the company earns. With the deal under review and shareholder lawyers circling, the real question for you is how firmly PTC's earnings base supports where the stock now sits.
Over the past 5 years PTC has delivered a total return of about 60.1%, which puts more pressure on today's valuation to be backed by the underlying earnings power rather than sentiment alone.

The agreed cash acquisition by Schneider Electric at US$205 per share and the suspension of regular earnings updates may concentrate attention on the durability and quality of PTC's profit stream that underpins that offer price.
The issue now is whether the current share price for PTC is adequately supported by its earnings profile when judged against the Fair Ratio benchmark.
If you want a second reference point while you weigh the PTC offer, a focused screen of 39 high quality undervalued stocks can be a useful starting list for deeper research.

The P/E ratio fits PTC because earnings are still the main yardstick investors use to weigh established software platforms with recurring revenue models. PTC trades on a P/E of about 20.5x, which is below both the broader software sector on roughly 30.6x and a peer group average near 38.9x. That puts the current tag at a discount to where similar businesses and close comparables change hands on earnings.

On this framework, the Fair Ratio benchmark, which blends PTC’s growth profile, profit margins, size and risk, points to a richer multiple than the market is currently paying. Because the Schneider Electric US$205 per share cash offer has frozen the usual quarterly guidance, this gap between a 20.5x P/E and higher peer and Fair Ratio markers becomes a cleaner signal that the existing price reflects a more cautious earnings outlook than those reference points imply. Schneider Electric stock slips as record Q3 meets PTC test
sum: Schneider Electric reported record third-quarter revenue on October 16, 2026, and raised its full-year target for the second time this year. The company cited broad demand across end markets and regions, with data centers remaining the main growth driver.

Schneider Electric's Q3 2026 revenue release shows revenue of 11.46 billion euros, up 16.9 percent organically and 17.9 percent on a reported basis from the year-earlier quarter. Energy Management revenue reached 9.615 billion euros and grew 18.8 percent organically, while Industrial Automation revenue rose 8.1 percent organically to 1.845 billion euros.

Data Center and Networks demand increased at a triple-digit rate globally, according to the company. Demand was broad across hyperscale, colocation, neo-cloud and edge customers, supporting strong momentum in prefabricated solutions, electrical distribution, protection and cooling.

Schneider Electric now targets organic adjusted EBITA growth of 18 percent to 21 percent in 2026, based on organic revenue growth of 12 percent to 14 percent and adjusted EBITA margin expansion of 100 to 120 basis points. The target implies an adjusted EBITA margin of 19.7 percent to 19.9 percent.

The planned PTC acquisition adds a separate execution issue. Schneider Electric announced the agreement on October 5, 2026, with closing anticipated by the third quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The company expects the transaction to deliver 250 million euros of cost synergies by the third year and approximately 800 million euros of revenue synergies.

Schneider Electric stock traded at 228.20 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:06 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026, down 1.60 percent against the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 4. That was 3.11 percent below the 235.53-euro quote in the relevant November 5 report at 11:17 CET, marking the latest measurable change for investors.

Schneider Electric stock weighs PTC bond financing
sum: Schneider Electric has added a major debt component to the financing of its planned acquisition of PTC. The French energy technology group launched a multi-tranche senior bond offering on October 26, 2026, and announced the completed issue on October 28 in a regulated release carried by Les Echos.

The senior notes total 6.0 billion euros and have an average maturity of 8.2 years with an average coupon of about 4.3 percent. The issue sits under Schneider Electric's Euro Medium Term Note program and is intended to help fund the purchase of PTC, a US provider of industrial design, engineering and data-management software.

The bond sale follows Schneider Electric's 6.0 billion euro capital increase, completed through an accelerated bookbuilding offering without preferential subscription rights for existing shareholders. Together, the measures form a financing package for a transaction that Schneider Electric agreed with PTC on October 5.

The bond structure spreads maturities from November 2028 to November 2046. It includes a floating-rate tranche linked to three-month Euribor plus 0.45 percent, while the fixed-rate tranches carry coupons ranging from 4.000 percent to 5.000 percent. The schedule gives investors several repayment dates but also leaves Schneider Electric with a long-dated interest burden.

Schneider Electric agreed to pay 205 US dollars in cash for each PTC share. The transaction values PTC's equity at approximately 22.6 billion US dollars and is intended to create a broader industrial software and artificial intelligence platform. Schneider Electric expects 250 million euros of annual run-rate cost synergies by the third year and approximately 800 million euros of revenue synergies.

The financing changes the investment debate from the strategic rationale alone to the returns generated after closing. Schneider Electric has said the acquisition should be accretive to adjusted earnings per share before purchase-price allocation effects, but the benefits depend on integration, financing costs and the delivery of the planned synergies.
Schneider Electric expects the transaction to close in the third quarter of 2027, subject to approval by PTC shareholders and regulatory clearances.

PTC Heads Into Q4 Earnings as Schneider Buyout Looms: What's in Store?
sum: PTC Inc. PTC is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 4, after market close.
For the fiscal fourth quarter, PTC estimates revenues in the $630-$690 million band. Non-GAAP EPS is projected in the range of $1.63 to $2.21.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $657.6 million, down 26.4% from the year-ago reported number. The consensus estimate for earnings is pegged at $2.00 per share, down 42.4% from a year ago.
The company’s earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters, while missing once, with the average earnings surprise being 25.9%.

PTC’s fiscal fourth-quarter performance is likely to have been aided by recurring revenue growth, demand for product lifecycle management (PLM) and computer-aided design (CAD) software, AI-related opportunities and cash flow momentum.

In October, PTC announced that it had entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by Schneider Electric for $205 per share in cash, valuing PTC’s equity at approximately $22.6 billion. The transaction is expected to create a scaled industrial software and AI platform, with Schneider Electric targeting €250 million in annual cost synergies and approximately €800 million in revenue synergies. Following this development, PTC suspended its quarterly earnings conference calls and stopped providing quarterly and annual financial guidance.

PTC continues to see solid demand across its go-to-market initiatives and encouraging early traction for its AI offerings. Supported by strong momentum and promising growth opportunities, the company is likely to have entered the fiscal fourth quarter on solid footing and raised the midpoint of its full-year ARR growth guidance to 9.25%, reflecting confidence in its ability to deliver a strong finish to the year. PTC raised and narrowed its full-year ARR guidance, with the midpoint implying $214 million in net new ARR, reflecting strong go-to-market execution and improved pipeline visibility. It expects a boost in the fiscal fourth quarter, supported by healthy demand generation and the conversion of deferred ARR, with net new ARR (excluding Kepware and ThingWorx) projected at $79-$92 million.

GE Vernova Buys Trench Group for $9 Billion, Raises 2026 Revenue Outlook - News and Statistics
sum: GE Vernova has struck a $9 billion deal to acquire high-voltage equipment manufacturer Trench Group from Triton Partners, while simultaneously raising its 2026 revenue projection for the third time.
The company now anticipates revenue between $46.5 billion and $47.5 billion for the year, an upward revision from the $45.5 billion to $46.5 billion range provided in July guidance.

Trench manufactures high-voltage grid equipment, a market gaining momentum as utilities boost spending to modernize aging infrastructure and accommodate demand tied to data centers and industrial electrification. The acquisition brings Trench's Charlotte facility, where 765-kilovolt equipment production is set to commence in late 2027, plus a backlog valued at approximately $5 billion and an expanded presence across Europe and Asia.

GE Vernova projects Trench will deliver roughly $1.9 billion in revenue by 2028 with an adjusted EBITDA margin near 36%, and generate $50 million to $100 million in yearly cost savings by 2030. The purchase will be financed equally through cash and debt, with completion targeted for late 2027. CEO Scott Strazik valued the global high-voltage market at $130 billion by the decade's end.

Third-quarter orders surged 96% to $29.3 billion, pushing the backlog to an all-time high of $197 billion, up from $176 billion three months prior. Power orders nearly tripled amid gas turbine demand, and the company is already accepting reservations for 2031 delivery. Revenue grew 27%, Electrification revenue jumped 51%, and adjusted EBITDA of $1.94 billion surpassed analyst expectations compiled by LSEG.

GE Vernova now forecasts a 2026 wind EBITDA loss of $400 million to $500 million, versus approximately $400 million projected in July. The segment posted $72 million in third-quarter earnings, compared with a $61 million loss during the same period last year. The company also lowered its 2026 tariff cost estimate to under $100 million.

Schneider Electric (ENXTPA:SU) Stock May Be Near Fair Value After AI Demand Surge
sum: Schneider Electric has had a powerful three year share price run, yet a recent pullback raises a sharper question for investors about how far its current market value is supported by the cash the business is expected to generate. With the stock now trading around €249.10, the issue is whether that price still lines up with the cash flow profile implied by its recent projects and partnerships.
- Schneider Electric has returned 86.7% over the past three years. That makes it important to ask whether the recent share price level is still in line with what its cash flows can justify.

- Record high revenue supported by a global data center boom and triple digit demand growth in that segment can shape expectations for future cash generation and the timing of those inflows from long dated infrastructure projects.
- If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Schneider Electric's 29.6x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether Schneider Electric's current share price is justified by the cash flows implied by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of the business.
If you are weighing Schneider Electric against other ways to play the same infrastructure and AI build out, it can help to line it up beside 55 AI infrastructure stocks.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here is built around the cash Schneider Electric is expected to generate for shareholders over time. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about €5.7b, and the projections used in the model assume this pool of cash is growing rather than shrinking over the coming decade, then easing back to a more moderate pace.

Schneider Electric slides as J.P. Morgan sees PTC deal weighing on valuation
sum: Investing.com -- Shares in Schneider Electric fell by 3% on Tuesday after J.P. Morgan downgraded the energy management and industrial automation group to "neutral" from "overweight", saying its PTC and Cognite deals shift the investment case towards the less attractive Industrial Automation division.

The brokerage cut its December 2027 price target to €310 from €345 and lowered its target multiple to 18.5 times FY27 EV/EBITA from 20.5 times, reflecting its view of the company's evolving capital discipline.

J.P. Morgan's previous "overweight" view was based on organic growth in Schneider's Energy Management division, which accounts for about 85% of group profit. Analyst Phil Buller said the PTC deal weighs on the valuation multiple, despite potential benefits across the group.

Schneider agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal at $205 per share, valuing the software company at about $22.6 billion in equity value and $23.7 billion in enterprise value. The offer represents a 42.3% premium to PTC's previous closing price.
J.P. Morgan said the roughly $20 billion decline in Schneider's shares the previous day was "mathematically oversold" relative to the proposed deal's roughly $24 billion enterprise value.

It said the move was disproportionate, noting the stock had risen close to record highs after Schneider's Singapore presentation on its Energy Management portfolio and a bullish pre-close call. The shares are now at the same level as in mid-September, it said.

The brokerage described PTC as a good asset overall and expects the deal to close by the third quarter of 2027, as the companies have said, with limited risk from antitrust or regulatory approvals in China and the United States.

Schneider Electric shares plunge on record $22.6bn PTC deal
sum: French energy technology group Schneider Electric has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Boston-based PTC for $22.6bn (€20.1bn) to expand its industrial AI business. The French company's shares plummeted on Monday following the announcement.
Schneider Electric, one of Europe's most valuable companies, saw its shares plunge after confirming an agreement to buy US-based industrial design software company PTC.
The deal is expected to be the largest acquisition in Schneider Electric's history, as the company seeks to expand its industrial AI capabilities using product and engineering data.
The French energy technology group will pay $205 per share for 100% of PTC's shares in cash, valuing its equity at $22.6bn (€20.1bn) and the business, including debt, at $23.7bn (€21.1bn).

The deal "creates a leading, scaled, open and interoperable industrial software and AI franchise", Schneider said in a statement, adding that PTC's board had agreed to the deal. The offer represents a 42.3% premium to PTC's last closing share price.

Schneider said the deal would combine industrial software and AI to help customers design, manufacture, operate and maintain products more efficiently, using industrial data to guide decisions and improve performance.

Olivier Blum, chief executive of Schneider Electric, said: "The acquisition of PTC represents an important step forward in our ambition to lead the new era of Energy and Industrial Intelligence. Together, we are creating the industry’s most complete Software & AI powerhouse and highest-quality portfolio bridging the physical and digital worlds."

AI stocks fall after Amodei, Altman, and Musk back AI slowdown
sum: AI-linked stocks fell across Asia, Europe, and U.S. premarket trading on Monday after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a deliberate slowdown in AI capabilities development, drawing support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
Nvidia, Intel, ASML, SK Hynix, and SoftBank were among the hardest-hit names as investors weighed the implications of a deliberate cap on AI progress

Nvidia $NVDA stock fell nearly 3% in premarket trading, while Intel $INTC stock dropped close to 6% and Micron $MU Technology stock declined around 5%. In Asia, SK Hynix ended the session with losses exceeding 6%, while Samsung Electronics shed more than 4%. SoftBank stock, reflecting that company's position as one of OpenAI's largest investors, fell roughly 10% to 11% in Tokyo. South Korea's Kospi fell 3.3%. In Europe, ASML $ASML lost between 5% and 6%, Nokia gave up roughly 8%, and Infineon retreated more than 7%. Hyperscalers including Microsoft $MSFT, Amazon $AMZN, and Alphabet $GOOGL were lower in premarket trading. Data-center infrastructure plays Siemens Energy and Schneider Electric likewise moved lower.

Amodei published an essay on Saturday outlining a three-step plan he called "pacing the frontier," which would embed third-party evaluators inside AI companies, establish shared safety benchmarks and agreed limits on how fast capabilities can advance, and eventually coordinate with governments including China. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.

Altman posted on X $TWTR on Saturday saying he agrees with Amodei's call to pace the frontier. Musk posted on X that "Dario is right," according to CNBC. In a follow-up post just after midnight on Monday, Altman clarified that pacing does "not mean 'stopping,'" adding that "no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness."

Amodei's essay and the broader debate it reflects emerged from a turbulent stretch for the AI industry. Jacob Coxon, a researcher who had resigned from Anthropic last week, wrote that AI companies are "gambling with our lives," a post that drew more than 150 million views on X and prompted more than 20 lawmakers to call for tougher AI regulation.

With the market capitalization of Rs. 29,253 Crores, the shares of Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltdwere trading at around Rs. 1,223 per share which is 21 percent discount from its 52 week high of Rs. 1,548 per share and is trading at a P/E of 151 whereas industry P/E stands at 35

Management stated that more than one-fifth of the order bank now includes segments that are considered emerging, such as data centers and semiconductors. The organization wants to selectively increase the proportion of these segments while continuing to operate its core business. They also mentioned that customer engagement in these segments is quite strong.

In Q1, the company got a huge order for semiconductors front-end fab of digitally enabled transformers. Also, the company got an order from the data center that included MV panels, transformers, automation devices & panels.

Order intake in Q1 was ₹915 crore, which management referred to as the all-time high quarterly order booking. Order intake was higher by 0.5% compared to the same period last year, growing by double digit quarter-on-quarter. Order book reached ₹2,100 crore plus, higher by 33%.

According to management, the Q1 gross margin has been impacted by inflation in commodities and the legacy order book. The legacy orders were at fixed prices, but there have been rises in raw-materials' prices during execution. However, pricing actions have been undertaken to address raw-material inflation, and price variation clauses are being added where feasible. Previously, such clauses would be used for about 20-25% of orders.

Around ₹500 crore has been spent by the firm during the last three years in three plants: medium voltage plant in Baroda, Baroda transformer plant, and Kolkata plant. Expansions are progressing well with some capacity additions expected in CY27 and some in CY28 and beyond. Export sales are currently around 10-12% of sales, and management believes that export dollar value would rise going ahead with Kolkata plant capacity additions.

Smart City Market Size, Share, Trend | CAGR of 21.6%
sum: In 2025, the Global Smart City Market was valued at USD 1.4 trillion. The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 21.6% during 2026–2035, reaching approximately USD 10.2 trillion by 2035. North America dominated the global market in 2025, accounting for more than 22.0% of the total market share and generating approximately USD 384.3 billion in revenue.

Growth is mainly supported by rapid urbanization, rising infrastructure spending, and stronger government focus on digital public services. In 2018, UN DESA reported that 55% of the global population lived in urban areas and estimated that this share would rise to 68% by 2050. This shift will add nearly 2.5 billion urban residents, mainly across Asia and Africa, creating significant demand for modern transport, energy, water, waste management, housing, and public safety systems.

Urban infrastructure investment is also increasing rapidly. Annual physical capital investment in cities was expected to rise from around USD 10 trillion to more than USD 20 trillion by 2025. Total urban infrastructure requirements, including buildings, utilities, and transport networks, are estimated at approximately USD 80–97 trillion by 2040. If only 10–15% of this spending is directed toward connected and intelligent systems, the smart city market could reasonably exceed USD 10 trillion by 2035.

North America is supported by early adoption of 5G, IoT, smart grids, and data-based city management. Urbanization in several advanced economies is expected to exceed 80% by 2050, while infrastructure spending commonly represents 2–6% of GDP. As the global urban population increases from 4.2 billion to approximately 6.7 billion by 2050, demand for smart mobility, utilities, governance, and public services will continue to strengthen.
- The Smart City Market reached USD 1.4 trillion and is projected to grow at a 21.6% CAGR to approximately USD 10.2 trillion by 2035.
- Smart utilities dominated the application segment with a 29.5% share, supported by rising investment in electricity, water, and waste infrastructure.
- Hardware captured a leading 54% share, driven by demand for sensors, cameras, smart meters, controllers, and communication equipment.
